questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors
questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=7\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}-1=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =b \\ 2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=2\cdot 1=2.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=-2 \\ -4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 \\ -4 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ -4 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 \\ 3 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 \\ 0 & -3 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 31\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=31,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $b$ does *not* lie in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$

questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, ${a}_{3}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -14 \\ -14\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -14 \\ -14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=6 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=-14 \\ -3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-14\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ -3 & 1 & 6 & -14 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=6 \\ {x}_{2}=4 \\ {x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}-2(-2)=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}+(-2){a}_{3} & =b \\ 2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+4\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -14 \\ -14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=2\cdot 4\cdot (-2)=-16.$

$$

We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 3 & 2 & -5 \\ 2 & -1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 8 & -32 \\ 2 & -1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 8 & -32 \\ 0 & 3 & k-18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & k-18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & k-6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-6.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-6\,⇒\,k=6.

\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 5 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 6 & 12 \\ 2 & -1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 6 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & k+6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{6}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & k+6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & k+4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k+4.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+4\,⇒\,k=-4.
$$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,3,2⟩$, $c=⟨2,-1,-1⟩$, and  $u=⟨5,-5,-4⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+2t=5 \\ 3s-t=-5 \\ 2s-t=-4\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 2 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 2 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 0 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+2t=5 \\ t=2 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=2.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s+2t & =5 \\ -s+2(2) & =5 \\ -s+4 & =5 \\ s & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-1,\,t=2,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-b+2c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-1)\cdot 2=-2.$

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 10 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s-8t=6 \\ 7s+10t=9 \\ -3s-4t=-4\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 7 & 10 & 9 \\ -3 & -4 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 66 & -33 \\ -3 & -4 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 66 & -33 \\ 0 & -28 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{66}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & -28 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+28{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

{\begin{aligned}s-8t=6 \\ t=-\frac{1}{2} \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s-8t & =6 \\ s-8(-\frac{1}{2}) & =6 \\ s+4 & =6 \\ s & =2.\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We know that $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}$ if there exist $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=8 \\ {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-5\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 2 & 2 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -8 & -21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -8 & -21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+8{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0x_1 + 0x_2 = 3,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $\mathbf{b}$ does *not* lie in $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a_1}, \mathbf{a_2} \}.$

canonical_examples.problem: Determine if the vector $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\;\Pi \,:\, \mathbf{r}=s \mathbf{b} + t \mathbf{c}, \, t,s \in \mathbb{R},$ where  $\mathbf{b}=\langle 1, 4, 5 \rangle, \mathbf{c} = \langle 2, 4, 6 \rangle$ and  $\mathbf{u}= \langle 2, 10, 12 \rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{u} \in \Pi$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 10 \\ 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s+2t=2 \\ 4s+4t=10 \\ 5s+6t=12\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 4 & 10 \\ 5 & 6 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 5 & 6 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}s+2t=2 \\ -4t=2 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
-4t = 2 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad t = -\dfrac{1}{2}.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s+2t & =2 \\ s+2(-\frac{1}{2}) & =2 \\ s-1 & =2 \\ s & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=3, \, t=-\dfrac{1}{2},$ we conclude that $\mathbf{u}$ does indeed lie on the plane $\Pi.$ In fact, we have

$$
\mathbf{u}=3\mathbf{b} - \dfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{c}.
$$
